_comment: Cached Figma variable/node IDs for the wend-ui file, so use_figma pushes and diffs can reference known IDs instead of re-discovering them via a fresh read every time. IDs are stable in Figma once created -- this only goes stale if a variable/node is renamed or deleted outside this workflow. Regenerate with figma-scripts/dump-variable-map.js (paste its contents into a use_figma call) whenever collections change, and spot-check a few IDs with getVariableByIdAsync before trusting a map that's more than a few sessions old.

global._naming_note: Naming is inconsistent by when each variable was added, not by any semantic rule: the original gray-25..600 and most spacing/radius/font-* steps use slash-style (color/gray/25, spacing/100), while gray-700..1000 and every amber/green/red step added later use dash-style (color-gray-700, color-amber-500). Code's own token names are always dash-style (color-gray-*), so a diff_tokens comparison against this collection's slash-named entries will report those as onlyInProject/onlyInFigma purely from the naming mismatch even when the resolved hex is identical -- normalize slashes to dashes before diffing (see sync-tokens-to-figma skill). color-green-500/color-red-500 (the dark-mode feedback shades) now live in this collection's variableIds normally -- the prior '_orphaned, detached from variableIds' state noted here as of 2026-08-03 no longer applies as of this refresh.
global._size_note: sizing/0..sizing/3200 (VariableID:357:2 through :357:22, added 2026-08-23 as size/*, renamed in place to sizing/* the same day -- IDs unchanged) is a new code-originated scale, pushed FROM tokens/global/sizing.json TO Figma -- the reverse direction of most entries in this cache. It deliberately duplicates spacing/*'s step names and px values 1:1 (same ALL_SCOPES convention, same slash-style naming) rather than aliasing spacing, per packages/tokens/README.md's Sizing scale section: kept separate so width/height and padding/gap can diverge later even though they're numerically identical today. No Figma component currently binds to sizing/* -- it exists so future width/height properties have a token to reach for.
global._owner_note: sizing/* is the one entry in this collection code created rather than pulled -- everything else here originated in Figma and was pulled into code. Don't assume push-then-verify (steps 2-3 of sync-tokens-to-figma) is unnecessary just because this collection is 'usually' Figma-authoritative.

semantic._naming_note: Mixes dash-style (color-text-secondary) and slash-style (color/action/primary-background) by when each variable was added -- same caveat as the global collection's naming note. color/ui/text/disabled and color/ui/text/primary are a separate, divergent pair from code's color-text-disabled/color-text-primary: 'disabled' is a pure rename with an identical value (safe to treat as the same token under a different name), but 'primary' also carries a different color value than what code currently ships (code pulled the value update but deliberately did NOT adopt the 'ui' name -- introducing a new 'ui' taxonomy category isn't registered in validate-color-taxonomy.js; see packages/tokens/README.md's Color scale section and the 2026-08-19 token-pull session notes). color/ui/outline/focus (VariableID:351:81, added 2026-08-23) is a third 'ui'-namespaced variable but WAS pulled into code, as color.border.focus (color-border-focus) under the existing 'border' SELF_EVIDENT_CATEGORY rather than adopting the 'ui' prefix -- same treatment as 'disabled' above, a rename-in-spirit with a code-side name that fits the existing taxonomy. color/ui/foreground and color/ui/border/default (VariableID:360:140, :347:4, both consumed by the new Checkbox component added 2026-08-23) are a fourth and fifth 'ui'-namespaced pair, also pulled into code -- as color.surface.input (color-surface-input) and color.border.input (color-border-input) respectively, again under existing SELF_EVIDENT_CATEGORYs rather than adopting 'ui'. spacing/default, spacing/condensed, spacing/compressed, spacing/expanded, and spacing/double exist in Figma with no corresponding token in code at all -- flagged during the same session, not yet pulled in.
semantic._state_note: color-action-primary-background-hover was seen at VariableID:49:59 as of this refresh; a much earlier state (pre-2026-08-03) had also recorded it at :49:58, which was actually color/action/primary-background -- if a future diff shows both resolving to the same collection but different keys, trust a fresh dump-variable-map.js run over this cached file.
semantic._drift_flag: As of the 2026-08-23 Checkbox pull, color/action/primary/background/default (VariableID:49:58) and color/action/primary/background/hover (VariableID:49:59) resolve to DIFFERENT values per mode in Figma (background/default: light gray-950 #333333, dark gray-700 #8D8B8B; background/hover: light gray-975 #1A1A1A, dark gray-600 #9A9898) -- this contradicts the 'every action.primary token is deliberately identical in light and dark mode' design decision documented in packages/tokens/README.md's Color scale section (color.action.primary.background/background-hover in code have NO dark override, i.e. still fixed both modes). This was NOT adopted into code -- the checkbox's checked-state tokens alias the existing fixed-both-modes action.primary tokens instead, so the checkbox will look consistent with buttons in code today but will NOT pixel-match Figma's dark-mode checked checkbox. Flagged for the user to decide (adopt the dark divergence app-wide for action.primary and update the README's 'buttons don't flip by theme' claim, or treat it as unintentional Figma drift) -- do not silently resolve either way in a future session.

nodes._comment: Canvas nodes bound to semantic/component variables or component properties -- useful when a collection rebuild requires rebinding fills/strokes/fontFamily/etc, or when re-touching the button's icon slots.
nodes._pages_note: As of 2026-08-23 the file has multiple pages (Button, Checkbox, Toggle, Radio, plus Cover/Typography/Color/Icons/reference pages not tracked here) -- the single 'page': "Button" field below predates that and is stale/button-specific; don't assume it names the only page. Page IDs: Button=10:2, Checkbox=347:2, Toggle=367:164, Radio=374:187 (also hosts the separate 'Radio Group' component, node 374:231, alongside the Radio COMPONENT_SET). Get a fresh list with `figma.root.children.map(p => ({id: p.id, name: p.name}))`.

radioGroup._note: Added 2026-08-23. A single (non-variant) COMPONENT, not a COMPONENT_SET -- lives on the same page as the base Radio component but is a separate top-level node (374:231), not a child of the Radio COMPONENT_SET (374:188). Structure: an optional 'Label' text node (font-size.175, color.text.primary -- same style as the group's own label prop in code) + 5 instances of the base Radio component (all placeholder 'Selected=False, State=Default', i.e. no example of a selected state), in a VERTICAL auto-layout frame with itemSpacing=16 (spacing/default=16=spacing.200) applied uniformly to every gap including label-to-first-radio. Each Radio instance exposes 'Show Label#360:32' (BOOLEAN, default true) as a component property on the base Radio component itself -- missed when wend-radio was first built, but not actually a functional gap: wend-radio already hides its label whenever the `label` prop is an empty string, which is equivalent in effect. wend-radio-group is NOT a literal transcription of this Figma node (which just shows 5 static radio instances) -- it's a data-driven wrapper: consumers slot in their own <wend-radio> children (native `shadow:false` Stencil components support <slot> content relocation despite not using a real shadow root), and the group propagates `name`/`disabled` and computes each child's `selected` by comparing its `value` to the group's own `value` prop, re-emitting a consolidated wendChange with the newly selected value whenever a child reports selection. Uses a native <fieldset disabled={disabled}> wrapper so the browser's own form-disabling cascades to the slotted <input>s as a functional safety net, in addition to code explicitly propagating `.disabled` to each wend-radio child for the correct visual (dimmed) treatment (native fieldset-disabling alone doesn't trigger wend-radio's own CSS dimming, which keys off its own `disabled` prop/class, not the native :disabled pseudo-class).

radio._note: Added 2026-08-23. 4 variants (Selected=False/True x State=Default/Hover), no Disabled -- same shape as checkbox (code added a disabled prop anyway, dimmed via CSS opacity, for family consistency; not Figma-verified). Same width/height (58x20 including label) and Label-node structure as checkbox, and reuses the same outer-ring tokens (color.surface.input / color.border.input, VariableID:360:140 / :347:4) -- but unlike checkbox, the outer ring is IDENTICAL across all 4 variants (verified: unselected-hover's ring has the exact same fill/stroke boundVariables as unselected-default), so color.radio.control has only ever needed a 'default' state, no 'hover' variant at all. The inner dot (12x12, bound to sizing/150 -- a real binding, unlike checkbox/radio's own 20px size which is NOT bound) only exists as a child node when Selected=True; code always renders it and toggles visibility via CSS `input:checked ~ .control .dot { visibility: visible }` rather than conditionally in JSX -- native radio-group deselection (browser unchecking a sibling <input> when another radio in the same `name` group is picked) does NOT fire a change event on the deselected sibling, so a JSX-conditional dot (the pattern used for checkbox's checkmark) would have gone stale showing a dot on a radio the browser already deselected. Label text color introduces a new semantic leaf, text.hover (VariableID:374:207, 'color/ui/text/hover' in Figma, light gray.950 dark gray.100) -- used for both the dot's hover fill AND the unselected-label's hover fill, but NOT for the selected-label's hover fill, which oddly reuses color.border.input (VariableID:347:4) instead -- replicated exactly as authored despite reading like a possible Figma authoring slip (a border-role variable used for text), not silently 'corrected' to text.hover for consistency.

toggle._note: Added 2026-08-23. 6 variants (State=Default/Hover/Disabled x On=False/True), no Disabled+Hover combo -- same coverage gap as checkbox/button. No label/text node in any variant (unlike checkbox, which has one) -- code's wend-toggle is a bare switch, no label prop; if a labeled variant is wanted later, check whether Figma has been updated with one before inventing typography tokens for it. Track width(40)/height(24) and the checked-thumb size(18) are NOT variable-bound in Figma (verified via boundVariables) -- code stores them as literal px values in component/toggle.json rather than force-fitting them onto sizing-scale steps that happen to match numerically (unlike the unchecked-thumb size, 16px, which IS bound to sizing/200 and does alias it). The checked track's background/hover/disabled colors reuse the EXISTING color.action.primary.background/-hover/-disabled tokens (same ones button/checkbox already use) -- same known drift applies here as the checkbox _drift_flag below (Figma's action.primary tokens now resolve differently per dark mode than what's shipped in code; not adopted). The unchecked track's default/hover colors are new toggle-specific semantic leaves (action.toggle-unchecked.background/-hover, VariableID:369:167/:369:172) since there was no existing token to reuse for that role. Track border reuses color.border.input (same as checkbox); disabled border/thumb color reuses color.text.disabled (VariableID:231:11, the same variable already cached above as color/ui/text/disabled) rather than introducing a new token. The thumb's soft drop-shadow (color/gray/600, radius 4, offset 0/0) is present on every variant except Default-Off and Disabled-Off in Figma -- reproduced in CSS as a box-shadow shown on :hover (unchecked) and always when checked, which covers exactly those states without a new state axis in the token set.

checkbox._note: Added 2026-08-23. Only 4 variants exist (Checked=False/True x State=Default/Hover) -- no Disabled or Active/Focus variants in Figma. Code added a disabled prop (dimmed via CSS opacity, mirroring the button's pattern) and a :focus-visible ring (reusing color.border.focus) beyond what's in Figma, for accessibility parity with wend-button -- neither is Figma-verified, flag if Figma later adds explicit Disabled/Focus variants so code can be reconciled against real values instead of an inference. The unchecked box's fill/stroke bindings are IDENTICAL between Default and Hover states (both resolve to color/ui/foreground and color/ui/border/default) -- Figma has not yet differentiated an unchecked-hover appearance, so CSS has no unchecked:hover rule either; only checked:hover (background-hover) is styled, matching what's actually authored.

buttonComponentSetProperties._comment: Component property keys on the wend-button COMPONENT_SET (10:13), added 2026-08-19 to support icon-left/icon-right per component/button.json. Bind icon instance nodes' componentPropertyReferences to these keys, not to a guessed/re-derived name -- the trailing #id changes if the property is ever deleted and recreated.
buttonComponentSetProperties.label: Label#10:1

nodes._icon_only_note: As of 2026-08-23, the wend-button COMPONENT_SET (10:13, frame resized to height 1160 to fit the new row) has an 'Icon Only' boolean variant axis. Icon Only=True variants exist for Primary/Secondary/Tertiary x Default/Hover/Active/Disabled (36x36, size-[36px] hardcoded in the Figma layer -- code instead derives the square via button-icon-only-padding, VariableID:350:2, 10px on all sides around a 16px icon, since 8*2+16=32 didn't match the observed 36px box but 10*2+16=36 does), plus Destructive Primary/Secondary/Tertiary x Default/Hover only (matching those variants' existing non-icon-only state coverage -- no Active/Disabled states exist for any destructive variant in Figma or code). Destructive icon-only components were cloned from Primary/Default (347:5) at x=40/163, y=930 (Destructive Primary), 1004 (Destructive Secondary), 1078 (Destructive Tertiary); tertiary's fills array is empty (transparent) like its non-icon-only sibling.
nodes._variants_note: 10:13's other 11 variants (Hover/Active states, Tertiary, Destructive Primary/Secondary/Tertiary) aren't individually enumerated here, same as the pre-2026-08-19 state of this file -- discover by name (e.g. `set.children.find(c => c.name === 'Variant=Tertiary, State=Hover')`) rather than assuming an ID.
